submitted.summary: An explicit totient-orbit labeling realizes the 88-vertex four-stage nanostar, refuting the nonexistence conjecture under the contracted-hexagon interpretation specified in the paper.
submitted.body:
Under the **contracted-hexagon interpretation** of the nanostar recursion, the four-stage tree $D_4$ is a $G_\phi$-graph. The interpretation is supported by the source figures and the cited construction; it is not an explicit contraction definition in the source.

Take

$A=\{3,167,334,19577,31657,39154,63314,702085,983055,1048576,1123336,1975461,2370559,2633948,3352289,3561823,4182461,4741118,5019445,5866457,8031112,8364922,11732914\}$.

The iterated Euler-totient orbit of $A$, with the loop at 1 omitted and edges regarded as undirected, has 88 vertices and 87 edges. Its centre is 1024. The complete arithmetic table and adjacency-preserving isomorphism to $D_4$ are provided in the proof. Thus a single stage-4 realization negates the universal nonexistence assertion, with the stated interpretation.

**Complete proof and verification files:** [MathDB paper 2611.00051](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00051) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00051v1). The paper page includes `proof-sources.json` and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the proof and verification sources. The Lean endpoint is `R162.not_conjecture349177`.

The contribution is an explicit finite counterexample; no minimality, uniqueness, higher-stage theorem, or general realization method is claimed. This is AI-assisted work, not external journal peer review. The paper records the exact formalization, trust, interpretation, and prior-art limitations; no worldwide-priority claim is made.
